Surah At-Taghabun is Madani according to the majority, and al-Dahhak said it is Makki. Al-Kalbi said it is both Makki and Madani. It has eighteen verses. From Ibn 'Abbas it is narrated that Surat al-Taghabun was revealed in Makkah, except for some verses at its end, which were revealed in Madinah concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the harshness of his family and children, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ [At-Taghabun: 14] to the end of the surah. And from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except that on the locks of his head is written five verses from the opening of Surat al-Taghabun."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾ (1)

Already mentioned in another place.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Indeed Allah created the children of Adam believing and disbelieving, and He will restore them on the Day of Resurrection as believers and disbelievers.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri narrated: The Prophet (ﷺ) addressed us one evening and mentioned some of what would come to pass, and he said: "People are born in different classes. A man is born a believer, lives a believer, and dies a believer. A man is born a disbeliever, lives a disbeliever, and dies a disbeliever. A man is born a believer, lives a believer, and dies a disbeliever. A man is born a disbeliever, lives a disbeliever, and dies a believer."

Ibn Masʿud said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah created Pharaoh in his mother's womb a disbeliever, and He created Yahya ibn Zakariyya in his mother's womb a believer."

And in the Sahih, from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud: "Indeed one of you may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit or a fathom, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed one of you may act with the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit or a fathom, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it." Related by al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi, and in it there is no mention of the fathom (baʿ).

In Sahih Muslim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Saʿidi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, while he is of the people of the Fire. And indeed a man may do the deeds of the people of the Fire in what appears to people, while he is of the people of Paradise."

Our scholars said: The meaning is the connection of eternal knowledge to every object of knowledge, so what He knows, wills and decrees comes to pass. He may will a person's faith in all circumstances, and He may will it until a known time. Likewise with disbelief. It has been said that there is an omission in the statement: "So among you is a believer, and among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a wicked one," and it was omitted because the context indicates it; this was said by al-Hasan. Others said: there is no omission in it, because the intended point is the mention of the two extremes. A group of the people of knowledge said: Indeed Allah created the creation, then they disbelieved and believed. They said: the completion of the statement is "He who created you," then He described them, saying: "So among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer," like His saying, Exalted is He: "And Allah created every creature from water; of them are those who walk on their bellies..." [al-Nur: 45], the verse. They said: Allah created them, and the walking is their action. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl chose this view and said: If He had created them as believers and disbelievers, He would not have described them by their action in His saying "So among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer."

They argued with His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every child is born upon the fitrah; then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian," the hadith in full. It has already been discussed fully in "al-Rum" [see vol. 14, p. 24]. Al-Dahhak said: "So among you is a disbeliever" means one who is a disbeliever in secret and a believer openly, like the hypocrite; and "among you is a believer" means one who is a believer in secret and a disbeliever openly, like ʿAmmar and his kin. ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah said: "So among you is a disbeliever in Allah and a believer in the stars, and among you is a believer in Allah and a disbeliever in the stars," meaning regarding the matter of the weather-mansions (anwaʾ).

Al-Zajjaj said — and it is the best of the statements, and the one held by the Imams and the majority of the community — : Indeed Allah created the disbeliever, and his disbelief is an action of his and an acquisition (kasb), while Allah is the Creator of disbelief. And He created the believer, and his faith is an action of his and an acquisition, while Allah is the Creator of faith. The disbeliever disbelieves and chooses disbelief after Allah has created him, because Allah, Exalted is He, has decreed this for him and known it of him. It is not possible that from either of them there should come into being anything other than what He has decreed for him and known of him, for the existence of what is contrary to the decreed would be incapacity, and the existence of what is contrary to the known would be a change, and neither befits Allah, Exalted is He. In this there is safety from both compulsion (jabr) and free will (qadar), as the poet said:

O you who look into the religion, what is the matter?
Neither a qadar has been sound, nor is there jabr.

Sailan said: A Bedouin came to Basra and was asked: "What do you say about qadar?" He said: "It is a matter about which opinions have exceeded their bounds and about which those who differ have differed. What is obligatory is that we return what is unclear to us of its ruling to what has preceded of His knowledge."

**Qur'an 64:3** — "He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and He formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final return."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾. This has been discussed in more than one place (see vol. 6, p. 384 and vol. 7, p. (19)). That is, He created them in truth, with certainty, with no doubt about it. It was also said: the *bā'* here carries the meaning of *lām* (for), that is, He created them *for the truth*, which is that He recompenses those who did evil according to what they did, and recompenses those who did good with the best (reward).

(﴿And He formed you and perfected your forms﴾) This refers to Adam, peace be upon him, whom He created with His own hand as an honour to him; this is the view of Muqatil. The second view is that it refers to all creatures. The meaning of *taṣwīr* (forming) has already passed, namely that it is shaping and fashioning (see p. 48 of this part). If it is asked: how did He perfect their forms? It is answered: He made them the best and most beautiful of all animals in form, as evidence that a person does not wish that his form were other than what he sees of the other forms. And among the goodness of their form is that he was created upright, not bent over, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾ (al-Tin: 4) — as its explanation will come, God willing, Exalted is He (see vol. 20, p. (113)).

(﴿And to Him is the final return﴾) That is, the return, so He will recompense each soul according to its deeds.
It has been mentioned in more than one place. He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen, nothing is hidden from Him.

The address is to Quraysh, i.e., "Did the news of the disbelieving former nations not come to you?"

﴿So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾, i.e., they were punished.

﴿And for them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., one that causes pain. This has already been mentioned [see vol. 1, p. 198].

That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient, and Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy. (6)

That is, this punishment befalls them because of their disbelief in the messengers who came to them with "clear proofs" (bil-bayyinat), meaning evident evidences.

"Shall mere humans guide us?" They denied that a messenger could be a human being. The word abasharun (أَبَشَرٌ, "mere humans") is in the nominative as the subject of a nominal sentence (mubtada', the inchoative). It is also said that it is governed by an omitted verb (idmar fi'l, an implied verb). The plural is used in the sense of the singular basharun (بَشَرٌ, "human"), which is why they said yahduna-na (يَهْدُونَنا, "guide us") and did not say yahdina (يَهْدِينَا). A singular noun may be used in the sense of the plural and function as a collective noun (ism al-jins), whose singular is insan (إِنْسَانٌ, "human being") and has no singular form from its own root. A plural may also be used in the sense of the singular, as in the Almighty's words: ﴿This is not a human being﴾ [Yusuf: 31].

"So they disbelieved": that is, by this statement, since they said it out of contempt, and did not know that Allah sends whom He wills to His servants. It is also said: they disbelieved in the messengers, turned away from the proof, and turned aside from faith and admonition.

"And Allah was self-sufficient": that is, by His dominion He is independent of the obedience of His servants. This was said by Muqatil. It is also said: Allah was self-sufficient through the evidence He manifested to them and the clear explanation He made plain to them, so He needed no further addition that would call them to right guidance or lead them to direction.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected.﴾ That is, they supposed (ẓannū). Al-zaʿm (claiming) is saying something on the basis of supposition. Shurayh said: "Every matter has a kunya (a metaphorical name), and the kunya of falsehood is 'they claim' (zaʿamū)." It was said: it was revealed concerning al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmi together with Khabbab, as its explanation has already preceded at the end of surah "Maryam" [[See vol. 11, p. 145.]]. Then it became general to every disbeliever.

(Say) O Muhammad: (﻿﻿"Yes, by my Lord, you will certainly be resurrected") That is, you will certainly be brought forth from your graves alive.

(Then you will certainly be informed) you will certainly be told

(of what you did) that is, of your deeds.

(And that is easy for Allah) since restoration is easier than initial creation.

**Qur'an 64:8:** ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. He commanded them to believe after He had informed them of the Hour's occurrence.

(And the light which We sent down) This is the Qur'an, and it is a light by which one is guided out of the darkness of misguidance.

(And Allah is Acquainted with what you do).

**First issue:** His saying, ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾. The governing element (al-'amil, the word that governs the grammar) in ﻳَﻮْﻡَ (yawma, "the Day") is either ﻟَﺘُﻨَﺒَّؤُﻥَّ ("you will surely be informed"), or the object of a verb implied by the sense of promise in the sentence, as if He said: "Allah will recompense you on the Day He gathers you." Or it is governed by an implied verb, "remember." Al-ghabn (ٱلْغَبْن) means loss. It is said: "He defrauded him (ghabanahu) when he took something from him for less than its value."

The recitation of the common readers is ﻳَﺠْﻤَﻌُﻜُﻢْ with the ya' (ي), because of His saying, ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾, which uses the third person, and because the name of Allah was mentioned first. Nasr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, al-Jahdari, Ya'qub and Salam recited ﻧَﺠْﻤَﻌُﻜُﻢْ with the nun (ن), in line with His saying, ﴿and the light which We have sent down﴾.

"The Day of Gathering" is the day on which Allah gathers the earliest and the latest generations, humans and jinn, and the people of the heavens and the people of the earth. It was also said: it is the day on which Allah joins each servant with his deeds. It was also said: it is called so because the wrongdoer and the wronged are gathered together on it. It was also said: because on it every prophet is gathered with his community. It was also said: because on it the reward of the people of obedience and the punishment of the people of disobedience are gathered together.

﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾: that is, the Day of Resurrection. A poet said:

"What do I hope for in life in a house of separation?
Certainly, comfort is only on the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain."

The Day of Resurrection is called the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain (yawm al-taghabun) because the people of Paradise defraud the people of the Fire: the people of Paradise take Paradise, and the people of the Fire take the Fire, by way of exchange. The loss arises from their exchanging good for evil, the excellent for the inferior, and bliss for punishment. It is said: "I defrauded so-and-so" when I traded with him or bought from him, so the loss falls on him and the gain is yours. The same applies to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, as will be explained. It is also said: "I defrauded the garment (ghabantu al-thawb) and khabantuhu" when it became longer than your measure, so you cut off part of it, and that is also a loss.

Al-maghabin (ٱلْمَغَابِن) are the folds of the body, such as the armpits and the thighs. The exegetes said: the one who is defrauded (al-maghbun) is the one whose family and dwellings in Paradise are taken from him. On that day the loss of every disbeliever will be manifest, through abandoning faith, and the loss of every believer, through his shortcoming in doing good and his squandering of his days. Al-Zajjaj said: the one who defrauds is the one whose rank in Paradise is raised above the one who is beneath his rank.

**Second issue:** If it is asked: what transaction took place between them such that loss occurs in it? It is answered: this is a representation of loss in buying and selling, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16] (see vol. 1, p. 210). When He mentioned that the disbelievers bought error in exchange for guidance, and that they did not profit in their trade but lost, He also mentioned that they were defrauded, for the people of Paradise bought the Hereafter by abandoning this world, and the people of the Fire bought this world by abandoning the Hereafter. This is a kind of exchange, in a broad and metaphorical sense. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has divided creation into two groups: a group for Paradise and a group for the Fire. The dwellings of all of them are set in Paradise and the Fire. Abandonment (khidhlan) may precede a servant, as we have explained in this surah and elsewhere, so that he becomes one of the people of the Fire. Thus the one granted success obtains the dwelling of the forsaken, and the dwelling of the one granted success in the Fire goes to the forsaken. It is as though an exchange took place, and so the loss occurred. Parables are set forth to clarify the wisdoms of language and of the Qur'an. All of this is gathered from the scattered reports and has come in fragmented form in this book. This exchange is also described as inheritance, as we explained in ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1] (see vol. 12, p. 108). And Allah knows best.

Mutual loss may occur on other days too, as will be explained later, but He intended the loss for which there is no compensation because of its finality.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "We have been told that mutual loss is of three kinds:
A man who knows a knowledge, teaches it, but himself neglects it and does not act upon it, so he is wretched because of it, while the one he taught acts upon it and is saved by it.
A man who acquires wealth from sources for which he will be questioned, and is stingy with it, neglects obedience to his Lord because of it, does no good with it, and leaves it to an heir for whom there is no accountability, so that heir uses it in obedience to his Lord.
A man who has a slave; the slave acts in obedience to his Lord and is made happy, while the master acts in disobedience to Allah and is made wretched."

It is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah, the Exalted, will set up a man and a woman before Him on the Day of Resurrection. Allah, the Exalted, will say to them a word; what will you two say? The man will say: 'O Lord, You made her maintenance obligatory upon me, and I acquired it from lawful and unlawful means, and these adversaries demand it, and I have nothing left with which to pay.' The woman will say: 'O Lord, what could I say? He acquired it unlawfully, and I ate it lawfully, and he disobeyed You for my sake, and I was not pleased with him for that.' So it will be said: 'Far away from him, and destruction!' Allah, the Exalted, will say: 'You have spoken truly.' He will be commanded to the Fire, and she will be commanded to Paradise. She will look down upon him from the levels of Paradise and say to him: 'We have been defrauded, we have been defrauded! We are made happy by what you have made wretched.'" That is the Day of Mutual Loss.

**Third issue:** Ibn al-'Arabi said: Our scholars (ulama'una) have argued from His saying, ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾, that loss is not permitted in worldly transactions, because Allah restricted mutual loss to the Day of Resurrection when He said, ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾. This restriction indicates that there is no loss in this world. So whoever discovers a loss in a sold item has the sale annulled if the loss exceeds one third. The scholars of Baghdad adopted this view and argued for it with several points. Among them is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying to Hibban ibn Munqidh: "When you trade, say: 'No deception' (la khilaba), and you have the option for three days." (Al-khilaba: deception.) This has a lengthy discussion that we have explained in the book of Disputed Questions (masa'il al-khilaf). Its essence is that loss in this world is prohibited by consensus (ijma') in religious law, since it is a form of forbidden deception (khida' muharram), which is prohibited in every religious community. However, a slight amount of it cannot be avoided by anyone, so it stands in sales, because if we ruled that it must be annulled, no sale would ever be valid, since no one is free of it. But when it is great, it can be avoided, so annulment because of it becomes obligatory. The distinction between the small and the great is a well-known principle of the Shari'ah, so our scholars set one third as the limit, having seen it applied in bequests and elsewhere.

On this reading, the meaning of the verse is: "That is the Day of Mutual Loss, which is permissible without any detail." Or: "That is the Day of Mutual Loss that can never be made up." This is because the mutual loss of this world can be made up in two ways: either by a return (radd) in some circumstances, or by profit in another sale and another commodity. But as for one who has lost Paradise, there is no recovery for him ever.

Some scholars of the Sufis said: Allah has ordained loss upon all creatures, so no one meets his Lord except as one defrauded, because he cannot fully complete his deed until he has fully received his reward. And in a report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one meets Allah except regretful: if he was a wrongdoer, because he did not do good; and if he was a doer of good, because he did not increase it."

**His saying, the Exalted:** ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him into gardens﴾. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir recited ﻧُﻜَﻔِّﺮْ and ﻧُﺪْﺧِﻠْﻪُ with the nun in both places, and the rest recited them with the ya' (ي).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally; and wretched is the destination.﴾ When He mentioned what is for the believers, He mentioned what is for the disbelievers, as has preceded in more than one place.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning by His will and His decree. Al-Farra' said: He means "except by the command of Allah." It was also said: "except by the knowledge of Allah." It was also said: the occasion of its revelation was that the disbelievers said: "If what the Muslims are upon were true, Allah would have protected them from calamities in this world." So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that whatever calamity befalls, whether to a person's self, wealth, speech or action, which entails distress or brings about punishment, whether swift or deferred, happens by the knowledge and decree of Allah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾, meaning he affirms and knows that no calamity befalls him except by the permission of Allah.

(He guides his heart) to patience and contentment. It was also said: He keeps him firm in faith. Abu 'Uthman al-Jizi said: whoever's faith is sound, Allah guides his heart to following the Sunnah. It was also said: "And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart" at the time of calamity, so that he says: ﴿Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 156], as said by Ibn Jubayr. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that Allah places certainty in his heart, so that he knows that what befell him was not going to miss him, and that what missed him was not going to befall him. al-Kalbi said: it means that when he is tested he is patient, when he is blessed he is grateful, and when he is wronged he forgives. It was also said: He guides his heart to attaining reward in Paradise. The common reading is "yahdi" with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dal, because the name of Allah is mentioned first. al-Sulami and Qatadah read "yuhda qalbuhu" with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dal, as a passive verb, and the ba' is in the nominative, because it is a verb whose subject is not named (nā'ib al-fa'il, the deputy of the agent).

Talha ibn Musarrif and al-A'raj read "nahdi" with a nun, as an expression of majesty, with "qalbahu" in the accusative. 'Ikrimah read "yahda'u qalbuhu" with a silent hamza and the ba' in the nominative, meaning it becomes still and reassured. Malik ibn Dinar read the same, except that he softened the hamza.

(And Allah is Knowing of all things) nothing is hidden from Him: the submission of one who yields and submits to His command, and the aversion of one who dislikes it.

Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance (of the message). (64:12)

Allah – there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely. (64:13)

That is: make the calamities easy upon yourselves, occupy yourselves with obedience to Allah, act by His Book, and obey the Messenger by acting upon his Sunnah. If you turn away from obedience, then upon the Messenger there is nothing but conveyance (al-tabligh).

(Allah, there is no deity except Him) That is: there is no one worthy of worship besides Him, and no creator other than Him; so rely upon Him alone.

Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance (of the message). (64:12)

Allah – there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely. (64:13)

That is: make the calamities easy upon yourselves, occupy yourselves with obedience to Allah, act by His Book, and obey the Messenger by acting upon his Sunnah. If you turn away from obedience, then upon the Messenger there is nothing but conveyance (al-tabligh).

(Allah, there is no deity except Him) That is: there is no one worthy of worship besides Him, and no creator other than Him; so rely upon Him alone.

There are five issues in this verse.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: This verse was revealed at Medina concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the harshness of his family and his child, so it was revealed. Al-Nahhas mentioned it. Al-Tabari related it from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: The whole of Surat al-Taghabun was revealed at Mecca except these verses: "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you," which were revealed concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who had a family and children, and whenever he wanted to go on a military expedition, they wept before him and softened him, saying: "To whom will you leave us?" So he would relent and stay behind, and then this was revealed: "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you."

The whole verse was revealed at Medina concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, and the remaining verses up to the end of the surah were revealed at Medina. Al-Tirmidhi related from Ibn 'Abbas, when a man asked him about this verse, "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them," that he said: These were men from among the people of Mecca who embraced Islam and wanted to come to the Prophet (ﷺ), but their spouses and children refused to let them go to the Prophet (ﷺ). When they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and saw that the people had gained understanding in the religion, they intended to punish them, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them," the verse. He said: This is a hadith that is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (sound).

The second: Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: This explains the aspect of enmity, for the enemy is not an enemy in his essence but is an enemy by his action. So when the spouse and the child commit the act of an enemy, they become an enemy, and there is no act more hateful than preventing the servant from obedience. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Satan sat in wait for the son of Adam on the path of faith and said to him: 'Will you believe and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers?' He disobeyed him and believed. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of emigration and said: 'Will you emigrate and leave your wealth and your family?' He disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of jihad and said: 'Will you strive and be killed, so that your wives are wed and your wealth is divided?' He disobeyed him and strove, and was killed, so it is binding upon Allah to admit him into Paradise." The sitting of Satan takes two forms: one of them is by whispering, and the second is by his being moved to what he wants through that spouse, child and companion. Allah, exalted is He, said: "And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them" [Fussilat: 25]. In the wisdom of 'Isa, peace be upon him: "Whoever takes a family, wealth and a child becomes a slave of the world." In the sound hadith there is an explanation of something lower than this in the condition of the servant. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wretched is the slave of the dinar, wretched is the slave of the dirham, wretched is the slave of the khamisa, wretched is the slave of the qatifa; if he is pricked with a thorn, may he not have it removed." And there is no baseness greater than worshipping the dinar and the dirham, and no aspiration lower than an aspiration that is raised by a new garment.

The third: Just as a man may have his child and spouse as an enemy, so too a woman may have her husband and child as an enemy, in this very same sense. The generality of His saying "from your spouses" includes the male and the female, since both are included in every verse. And Allah knows best.

The fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so beware of them﴾, its meaning is "for your own sake." Caution for the sake of oneself is of two kinds: either due to harm to the body, or due to harm to the religion. Harm to the body pertains to the world, and harm to the religion pertains to the Hereafter. So Allah, glorified is He, warned the servant against that and cautioned him about it.

The fifth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you pardon, overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Al-Tabari related from 'Ikrima concerning His saying, exalted is He: "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them," that he said: A man would want to come to the Prophet (ﷺ), and his family would say to him: "Where are you going, leaving us?" He said: So when he embraced Islam and gained understanding, he said: "I will certainly return to those who used to forbid this matter, and I will certainly do and I will certainly do," so Allah, exalted and mighty is He, revealed: "And if you pardon, overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." And Mujahid said concerning His saying, exalted is He: "O you who have believed, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them," that he said: They did not oppose them in the world, but their affection for them led them to take forbidden things for them, and they gave them to them. The verse is general in every act of disobedience that a person commits because of family and children. The specific occasion of revelation does not prevent the generality of the ruling.

Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 64, verse 15:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾. That is, a test and an examination that drives you to earn what is forbidden and to withhold the right of Allah the Exalted. So do not obey them in disobedience to Allah.

There is a hadith: "A man will be brought forward on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: 'His dependants consumed his good deeds.'" And it is related from one of the early generations (al-salaf): "Dependants are the woodworm of acts of obedience."

Al-Qutaybi said: *fitna* here means *ighram* (a consuming passion). It is said: "The man was seduced (futina) by the woman," meaning he was infatuated with her. It was also said that *fitna* means *mihna* (an ordeal). From this is the saying of the poet:

"The people have been tested in their religion, and Ibn Affan has left a long evil."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "None of you should say, 'O Allah, protect me from trial (fitna).' For there is none of you who returns to wealth, family and children without being involved in some trial. Rather, let him say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from misleading trials.'"

Al-Hasan, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you﴾, said: the particle *min* (among) is used for partition, because not all of them are enemies. He did not use *min* in the verse ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, because they are never free of trial and of the heart being preoccupied with them.

Al-Tirmidhi and others related from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) delivering a sermon when al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) came, wearing two red shirts and stumbling as they walked. The Prophet (ﷺ) came down, carried them before him, and then said: 'Allah the Mighty and Majestic has spoken the truth: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾. I looked at these two boys stumbling as they walked, and I could not be patient until I interrupted my speech and lifted them up.'" Then he resumed his sermon.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah has with Him a great reward﴾. That is, Paradise, which is the ultimate goal. According to the statements of the exegetes (mufassirun), there is no greater reward than it.

In the two Sahihs, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari, it is related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah says to the people of Paradise, 'O people of Paradise!' They will say, 'At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure.' He will say, 'Are you content?' They will say, 'And why would we not be content, when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation?' He will say, 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They will say, 'O Lord, and what is better than that?' He will say, 'I shall let My pleasure descend upon you, and I shall never be displeased with you after this.'" This has been mentioned earlier, and there is no doubt that contentment (al-rida) is the ultimate of hopes.

The Sufis recited, in confirmation of this:

"Allah tested His creatures with it; the Fire and the Garden are in His grip.
His estrangement is greater than His Fire, and His union is sweeter than His Garden."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 16–17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves.﴾ On this there are five issues.

The first: A group of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) held that this verse abrogates (nasikh) the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102] [[see vol. 4, p. 157]]. Among them were Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. al-Tabari mentioned: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102], he said: "A severe command came, and they said: 'Who can know the measure of this, or reach it?' So when Allah knew that this had become difficult for them, He abrogated it for them and brought this other verse, saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able.﴾" It was also said: it is muhkam (decisive), with no abrogation in it. Ibn 'Abbas said concerning the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102]: "It was not abrogated; rather, 'as He should be feared' means that one strives for Allah as He should be striven for, that no blame of any blamer takes them in (the matter of) Allah, and that they uphold justice for Allah even against themselves, their fathers and their sons." This has already been discussed [[see vol. 4, p. 157]].

The second: If it is said: if this verse is muhkam and not abrogated, what is the meaning of His saying in Surat al-Taghabun: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, and how is it permissible to combine the command to fear Allah as He should be feared with the command to fear Him as much as we are able? The command to fear Him as He should be feared is an unrestricted obligation of the Qur'an, without specification or conditional link, whereas the command to fear Him as much as we are able is a command to fear Him linked to a condition. It was answered: His saying ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ is far from what is indicated by His saying ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102]. What He meant by ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ is: "So fear Allah, O people, and be mindful of Him regarding what He has made a trial for you in your wealth and your children, lest their trial overcome you, and it turn you away from what is obligatory upon you for Allah, namely emigration (hijrah) from the land of disbelief to the land of Islam, so that you leave off emigration as much as you are able," meaning: while you are able to emigrate. This is because Allah, whose praise is great, had excused those who were unable to emigrate from leaving it, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves...﴾ up to His saying ﴿Then those — perhaps Allah will pardon them﴾ [al-Nisa': 97–99] [[see vol. 5, p. 354]]. He informed that He had pardoned those who had no means and were not guided to a way, by remaining in the abode of polytheism. Likewise, the meaning of His saying ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ regarding emigration from the abode of polytheism to the abode of Islam is: that you not leave it through the trial of your wealth and children. Among what indicates the soundness of this is that His saying ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ comes right after His saying: ﴿O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children there are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾. There is no disagreement among the early scholars of Qur'anic interpretation that these verses were revealed concerning a people of disbelievers who delayed emigration from the abode of polytheism to the abode of Islam, because their children discouraged them from it, as already mentioned. This is all the choice of al-Tabari.

It was also said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ refers to what one does voluntarily of supererogatory acts or charity. When the saying of Allah, may He be exalted, ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102] was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the people, so they stood (in prayer) until their ankles swelled and their foreheads were abraded. Then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed, as lightening for them: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, and the first was abrogated. This was reported by Ibn Jubayr. al-Mawardi said: It is possible, if this report is not established, that one who is compelled to disobedience is not held accountable for it, because he is not able to guard against it.

The third: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And listen and obey﴾, that is: listen to what you are admonished with, and obey in what you are commanded and forbidden. Muqatil said: "Listen," that is, pay attention to what is sent down to you of the Book of Allah, and this is the basic meaning of hearing. "And obey" His Messenger in what he commands you or forbids you. Qatadah said: "On this (listening and obeying) the Prophet ﷺ took the pledge of listening and obeying." It was also said: "And listen" means accept what you hear, and it was expressed by hearing because hearing is its purpose.

I say: Al-Hajjaj came upon this verse when he recited it and restricted it to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, saying: "So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey" — it belongs to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, the trustee of Allah and His caliph; there is no exception in it. By Allah, if I commanded a man to leave by the door of the mosque and he left by another, his blood would be lawful for me." He lied in its interpretation. Rather, it was first for the Prophet ﷺ, and then for those in authority after him. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾ [al-Nisa': 59] [[see vol. 5, p. 258]].

The fourth: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And spend﴾. It was said: this is zakat, as reported from Ibn 'Abbas. It was also said: it is voluntary spending. al-Dahhak said: it is spending in jihad. al-Hasan said: it is a man's spending on himself. Ibn al-'Arabi said: "The one who said this was misled by His saying ﴿for yourselves﴾, and he did not realize that spending in supererogatory and obligatory charity is a man's spending on himself. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, it is against them﴾ [al-Isra': 7] [[see vol. 10, p. 227]]. Every good that a man does is for himself." The correct view is that it is general. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that a man said to him: "I have a dinar?" He said: "Spend it on yourself." He said: "I have another?" He said: "Spend it on your dependants." He said: "I have another?" He said: "Spend it on your child." He said: "I have another?" He said: "Give it in charity." Thus he began with the self, the family and the child, and placed charity after that. This is the basic principle in the Shari'ah.

The fifth: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is better for yourselves﴾. "Khayran" is in the accusative by a hidden verb according to Sibawayh, indicated by "and spend," as if he said: "Seek in spending what is better for yourselves," or "Advance what is better for yourselves of your wealth." According to al-Kisa'i and al-Farra', it is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun, meaning: "Spend a spending that is better for yourselves." According to Abu 'Ubaydah, it is the predicate of a suppressed kana, meaning: "It will be better for you." Whoever makes the "good" refer to wealth, then it is accusative by "spend."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul — those are the successful﴾. The discussion of this has already passed [[see p. 29 of this part]]. Likewise: ﴿If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you﴾; its discussion has also passed in "al-Baqarah" [[see vol. 3, p. 237 and vol. 17, p. 242]] and Surat al-Hadid.

﴿And He will forgive you, and Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing﴾. The meaning of "shukr" has passed in "al-Baqarah" [[see vol. 1, p. 397]]. And "al-Halim" is the one who does not hasten.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 64, verse 18:

God's words, ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: that is, what is absent and what is present. ﴿And He is the Almighty (al-'Aziz)﴾: that is, the Overpowering, the Subduer. So it is among the attributes of acts (sifat al-af'al), and from it is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the Wise﴾ [[see vol. 15 p. (232)]] [al-Jathiyah: 2], meaning: from God, the Subduer, the Perfecter, the Creator of things. Al-Khattabi said: It may also carry the meaning of nafasat al-qadr (the preciousness of rank). From it one says: 'azza ya'izzu (with a kasra on the 'ayn), so the meaning of al-'Aziz in this sense is that nothing is equal to Him and that there is no like unto Him. And God knows best.

﴿Al-Hakim (the Wise)﴾ in the management of His creation. Ibn al-Anbari said: al-Hakim is the one who makes things firm (al-muhkim) in creating them; it has been turned from the form mufil to the form fa'il. From it is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾ [[see vol. 8 p. 305]] [Yunus: 1], meaning the firmly-made (al-muhkam), so it has been turned from the form mufal to the form fa'il. And God knows best.
